_comment: A vocabulary line's grammar, as cases both renderers must agree on: lib/texparse.py parse_voc, voc_text and lib/tex2html.py render_voc (the reader and the PDF read the macros this way) and lib/vocline.js, which a video's player draws a macro line with. `runs` is what parse reads, `html` what render draws, `text` what flatten gives back, `macro` whether the line is a macro line (lib/chunkdiv.py is_macro_line, ParsehVocline.isMacro); a line that cannot be read has `error` instead, compared by CODE -- `groups` for a macro short of its braces, `unclosed` for a brace never closed -- because Python raises three kinds of error for the two. `lang` is a registry code: a \vb prints that language's two labels, and its words are isolated with its code and direction. Run by tests/test_vocline.py.

_entries: A vocabulary line cut into ENTRIES, for the vocabulary list (TO-DO 11.14): lib/texparse.py voc_entries and lib/vocline.js entries. Each \dw \vb \bw starts an entry, and a \pw that opens a stretch of the line (its start or after a ;); a \pw after other text stays in the meaning. `word` is what the entry is listed under, `rom` its romanisation, `head` the runs the reader prints for the word (a \vb with its stems), `meaning` the text after it up to the next ; or entry as plain text, `key` the comparison form (texparse.vocab_key: same key, same word). A line that cannot be read has `error`, as in `cases`.

entries._why: a plain line holds no entry
Persian: the Arabic keyboard's ي and ك, a ZWNJ and the vowel marks -- one word, keyed in the Persian spelling
Arabic: a \vb with its two labels, and a \pw inside a meaning stays in it
Arabic keeps ى and ي apart
a \vb's meaning goes on after its group, up to the next ;

_plain: A PLAIN-TEXT vocabulary line (a video glossed before the macros) cut into entries by its shape, for the vocabulary list (a0.6.3 G6): lib/texparse.py voc_plain_entries and lib/vocline.js plainEntries, given the chunk's own `text` and its transliteration `tr`. Fields as in `entries`; `kind` is plain, or vb for a verb written with its stems. A line it cannot read with confidence, and a note (//), has no entries. The content is made up for these tests, in the shapes real videos write.
